title: ew says /oo/
parentNote: Today is ew, and it says /oo/ — the same sound your child already has from moon, blue and tune. This is the fourth spelling of one sound, which is not a mistake in the course, it is just English: /oo/ has four common spellings and a child meets all of them in real books. The one that actually trips children up is not ew on its own, it is ew next to ow, because the letters look so alike. Grew and grow, flew and flow, blew and blow are all real pairs, and a child who is reading fast will swap them. If that happens, don't reread the whole word — point at the last letter and say "w or ew?". That is where all the information is. Say the day's words out loud together a few times; the ear learns this pair faster than the eye does.

activities.title: The seed that grew
activities.prompt: Watch out for grew and grow in this one. They are the same word at two times, and the end of the word is the bit that tells you.
lines: My father drew a line in the mud with a stick and said, "Set it in there."
It is a seed, a little brown seed, and it looks like a bit of grit.
"That will not grow," I said. But I set it in the mud, and I waited.
The rain came down. The wind blew. Not a thing came up.
A bird flew down to look at the mud, and I yelled at it to keep off.
Then, when I had all but stopped looking, a green bit stuck up out of the mud.
It grew all week. Then a cow got in at the gate and had a chew at the top of it.
I yelled. The cow went off. And the green thing grew back in three days.
By the end of the summer it is up past the top of the shed.
"This is news," said my mother. "This is big news."
All the street came to look at it, and Meg drew it on the path in chalk.
Then a green pod grew on it, and in the pod is a seed.
It is a little brown seed, and it looks like a bit of grit.
My father drew a line in the mud with a stick. "Set it in there," he said.
